validated_results.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association
validated_results.reason: Hospital-based case-control study of foods and beverages and incident urothelial (bladder) cancer that explicitly reports on milk consumption, although no numeric estimate for dairy is given in the abstract.

extraction.comparison_type: Milk consumption (higher vs lower intake); no quantitative contrast reported
extraction.population: Outpatients at Aichi Cancer Center Hospital

sample_size.excerpt: Subjects included 124 men and women (bladder cancer cases) with newly diagnosed cancers of the renal pelvis (n = 5), ureter (n = 6) or bladder (n = 113) and 620 age- and sex-matched, cancer-free outpatients (controls) presenting at the hospital in the period from 1994 to 2000.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 124 + 620 = 744

cases.excerpt: Subjects included 124 men and women (bladder cancer cases) with newly diagnosed cancers of the renal pelvis (n = 5), ureter (n = 6) or bladder (n = 113) and 620 age- and sex-matched, cancer-free outpatients (controls) presenting at the hospital in the period from 1994 to 2000.

comparison.excerpt: Coffee and milk consumption did not appear to exert any influence.

design.excerpt: We undertook a hospital-based case-control study at Aichi Cancer Center Hospital, Japan.
